slides.title: Behavioral Model 12 Data 1. Relevant and frequent
slides.text: Behavioral Model 12 Data 1. Relevant and frequent feedback about the adequacy of performance 2. Descriptions of what is expected of performance 3. Clear and relevant guides to adequate performance Information Knowledge 1. Systematically designed training that matches the requirements of exemplary performance 2. Placement Resources 1. Tools, resources, time and materials of work designed to match performance needs Instrumentation Capacity 1. Flexible scheduling of performance to match peak capacity 2. Prosthesis or visual aids 3. Physical shaping 4. Adaptation 5. Selection Incentives 1. Adequate financial incentives made contingent upon performance 2. Non-monetary incentives made available 3. Career-development opportunities 4. Clear consequences for poor performance Motivation Motives 1. Assessment of people’s motives to work 2. Recruitment of people to match the realities of situation INDIVIDUAL ENVIRONMENT

slides.title: Data • Don’t tell people how well they
slides.text: Data • Don’t tell people how well they are doing • Provide misleading info on how they are doing • Hide what is expected • Don’t guide performance Instrumentation • Design tools without consulting the users • Keep developers or engineers away from users Incentives • Pay poor performers the same as good performers • Punish good performers in some way • Don’t use non-monetary incentives Knowledge • Leaving training to chance • Let unskilled supervisor’s train • Make training irrelevant to the job • Make training difficult to get Capacity • Schedule work times for when people are not at their sharpest • Select the wrong people for the job • Don’t provide job aids Motives • Design futureless jobs • Arrange unpleasant work conditions • Give pep talks instead of incentives Behavioral Model Anti-Pattern

slides.text: 80/20 Rule Business analytics: The use of simpler analytics methodologies on past data. Advanced analytics: Everything else, including predictive analytics.
